title: Posting Hours for Late-Cancelled and Missed Visits on the Personal Services Plan
content:
Hours owed under the Personal Services Plan for a service order that was cancelled late or missed (a no-show) are posted by the Resident and Family Services desk once the cancellation or no-show is on record. They are posted one order at a time, beginning with the most recently recorded cancellation or no-show, against that order with its own draw basis — late cancellation or no-show — and the billing month of its service date. They are taken from the plan's available hours, or charged at the package's hourly rate beyond the allotment where no hours remain.

## The hours entry

Each posting is one hours entry for that cancellation on the plan's ledger:

| Situation on the plan | Entry posted against the order |
|---|---|
| Hours remain available on the plan | Hours drawn from the plan's available hours |
| No hours remain | Hours charged at the package's hourly rate beyond the allotment |

The entry carries the order number, the reason the hours are owed (late cancellation or no-show) and the billing month of the visit's service date.

## Basis questions

**Does the resident have to ask for the hours to be posted?** No. The desk posts them once the cancellation or no-show is on record.

**Where several orders await posting, which comes first?** The order with the most recently recorded cancellation or no-show; orders are posted one at a time.

## Invocation: `post_services_order_hours_8d682fe6`

**Capability.** The tool posts the personal service hours owed for one service order on a personal services account. One call books one entry dated today against the order: either hours taken from the plan's available hours, which lowers the hours available on the plan, or hours billed at the package's hourly rate because no hours remain, which raises the amount owed. The entry carries the order number, why the hours are owed and the billing month of the service date.

**How it is invoked.** `post_services_order_hours_8d682fe6` is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it and then calls it.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `services_plan_id` | Reference number of the personal services plan the order belongs to, as returned by the personal services plan lookup | Identifier |
| `order_reference` | The service order number exactly as shown on the order in the service order lookup | Verbatim, copied character for character with no change |
| `draw_basis` | Why hours are owed for the order | One enum value listed below |
| `event_type` | The kind of entry posted for the order | One enum value listed below |
| `billing_period` | The month of the service date | `YYYY-MM` |
| `hours` | The hours owed | Decimal hours to 2 decimal places, a positive number |
| `amount` | For an hours charge, the money billed in USD; 0.00 when the entry takes hours from the plan's available hours | USD to 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent |

Enum values of `draw_basis`: `service_delivered` (the visit took place); `late_cancellation` (the resident cancelled the visit too late); `no_show` (staff arrived and the resident declined the service or was absent).

Enum values of `event_type`: `services_hours_draw` (the hours are taken from the plan's available hours); `services_hourly_charge` (the hours are billed at the package's hourly rate because no available hours remain). The account's other entry kinds belong to other actions and are not meant for an order's hours: `services_package_fee_charge` is a monthly package fee; `services_hours_grant` is a monthly allotment; `services_hours_rollover` is hours carried into a month; `services_hours_expire` is hours lapsing; `services_hours_restore` is hours given back after a dispute; `services_alacarte_charge` is a separately priced service; `services_fee_charge` is a late or returned payment fee; `services_payment` is money received; `services_payment_return` is a payment reinstated unpaid; `services_credit` is a money credit.

**Return.** On success, a dictionary rendered as text with `status` set to `hours_posted`, `services_entry_id` (reference number of the new entry), `event_type` (the kind of entry booked), `hours` (2 decimal places), `amount` (USD, 2 decimal places, 0.00 for hours taken from the plan), `hours_available` (hours on the plan after the entry, 2 decimal places) and `account_balance` (amount owed in USD after the entry, 2 decimal places).
